title: Randomized run probability is length invariant
statement: Let a nondeterministic register machine with $m$ registers and $d$ Boolean oracles have state set $\Lambda$, input $x$, initial configuration $a$, and let $G$ be a configuration property. Suppose that for every choice word of length $N$, the run ends in a halted configuration, and at each earlier prefix where the run has not halted, its configuration satisfies $G$. If $N\le N'$, then for every decidable configuration property $R$, the probability that $R$ holds after a uniformly chosen length-$N'$ choice word equals the corresponding probability for a uniformly chosen length-$N$ choice word.
hypotheses_covered: Every length-$N$ choice word leads to a halted configuration
